Test-isolation defect in cli_init.rs, CORRECTED 2026-07-25 after the owner asked which side leaks. Production behaviour is CORRECT and out of scope: `vibe init` remembering last_author is the feature, and nothing in the command should change. The defect is test-side and has two halves of different severity. (a) READING - unconditional and live: all 11 tests in cli_init.rs isolate nothing but VIBE_NO_DEFAULT_REGISTRY (their local vibe() builder at :10-16), so the non-interactive author resolves out of the developer's REAL ~/.vibe/config.toml via prompts.rs:99-110 (--author -> user_config.init.last_author -> detect_git_author). Their behaviour depends on the machine - the same class that let cli_mcp_kind pass all day by accident. (b) WRITING - real but CONDITIONAL, not every-run as first reported: maybe_save_author (init/mod.rs:178) is called outside the `if interactive` branch so it runs every time, but prompts.rs:132 writes only when the computed author differs from the stored one. On this machine last_author is already set, so the tests read it, it matches, and nothing is written. On a fresh machine or in CI - last_author unset, `git config user.name` set - the first test run DOES write it into the real user config. Fix: give cli_init.rs the UserScratch treatment DRIFT-012 gave the other four files. SECURITY-RELEVANT, owner decision needed. F-057 was filed as a stray cache directory; it is more than that. search.rs:427 calls vibe_publish::token::load_token_for_host("github.com"), whose 4th precedence leg is <settings-dir>/github.publish.token - present on this machine. The full-scan test clears legs 2-3 by env but could not reach leg 4, so an un-isolated run attached the real publish token to its outbound request. Measured against a loopback listener recording header NAMES AND LENGTH ONLY, never the value: pre-fix the request carried an Authorization header of 47 bytes (Bearer + a 40-char token); under UserScratch there is no Authorization header at all. DRIFT-018 closed the leg. TWO THINGS REMAIN FOR THE OWNER: (a) whether the token ever reached a real host rather than a fixture endpoint - if any of these tests ever pointed at a live github.com, the secrets-hygiene rule is rotate first, investigate second; (b) residue on disk - ~/.vibe/search-cache/primary/ and secondary/ hold three JSON files dated 2026-05-06 whose payloads are verbatim cli_search.rs mock fixtures. Left in place deliberately: deleting the developer's files is not an executor's call. || INVESTIGATED AND CLOSED 2026-07-26 by the reviewer, on the owner asking for a code answer rather than a guess: NO ROTATION NEEDED - the token never left the machine. Proof by code path, not inference. search.rs:426 loads the token only AFTER detect_github_org(&reg.url) succeeds, and the request then goes to `api_base`, i.e. whatever VIBEVM_GITHUB_API_BASE says. Exactly one test reaches that path with a github.com registry - search_full_scan_finds_matching_packages_in_github_org (cli_search.rs:614) - and it sets VIBEVM_GITHUB_API_BASE to a 127.0.0.1 mock (:663) and removes both publish-token env legs. The other two --full-scan tests use a gitverse registry, which detect_github_org REJECTS before the token is loaded. The remaining fixture hosts are example.invalid (the reserved never-resolves TLD). So the 47-byte Authorization header DRIFT-018 measured went to the loopback mock, not to github.com. The defect was real and is fixed - a test that can pick up a live credential is one env-var default away from sending it somewhere real - but no exposure occurred. The github.com/vibespecs and gitverse.ru/vibespecs strings in the fixtures are registry URLs (the spec storage the owner named), used only to parse an org name. Residue in ~/.vibe/search-cache/ (three mock-fixture JSONs from 2026-05-06) still awaits the owner; it is his file to delete.

CLOSE-OUT BLOCKER, and the campaign's own Phase D authored it. ##BASELINE-RECORD (PROP-043 7.3, lines 421-423) asserts verbatim: 'Shipped: baseline.rs's BaselineUnit carries exactly these fields, with Baseline::load / store and the rescan CLI live.' Baseline::store DOES NOT EXIST. The only impl Baseline in baseline.rs is `load` (:172-179); the file defines no writer, and nothing in the workspace constructs or serialises a Baseline. The `store` that does exist is Cache::store (cache.rs:106) - a DIFFERENT type in the same crate, which is almost certainly what the eye landed on. That is the substring-lie pattern the WAL already warns about, striking a third time and this time inside the campaign's own correction. Two real consequences: (1) the Close-out step 'baseline.json written' (plan section 5) has NO TOOL - scan/check/report/mirror/weave/rescan/resume/gate is the whole `vibe progress` subcommand list, there is no baseline verb; (2) section 6's entire monthly recurrence consumes `rescan --baseline <prev>/baseline.json`, a file nothing in the tree can produce, so the recurrence loop has never been runnable end to end. Also a VERDICT CORRECTION: BASELINE-RECORD was flipped drift -> confirmed by commit 0064fd4a ('one parity row needed no ruling') on exactly this false evidence, so the ledger currently counts as confirmed a row that is not true. Fix direction: build the writer (a Baseline projected from the campaign verdict map, plus a `vibe progress baseline` subcommand) and then re-seal the verdict - NOT soften the spec, because close-out and section 6 recurrence both need the artefact.
